decisive_items: fever and erythema on trunk and extremities 3 days after receiving first dose of Moderna vaccine
response.rationale: The presentation best fits a post-vaccination multisystem inflammatory syndrome: fever, erythema, markedly elevated inflammatory markers, hepatosplenomegaly, renal/cardiac involvement, and thrombocytopenia with repeatedly negative SARS-CoV-2 PCR. It is broader than isolated myocarditis, coronary thrombosis, vasculitis, or thrombocytopenia alone.

rejected.why: Describes only the coronary thrombotic findings without accounting for the systemic febrile inflammatory syndrome.
Elevated troponin and CK support cardiac injury but do not explain rash, hepatosplenomegaly, renal defects, or arterial wall destruction.
Vasculitis is a plausible vascular mechanism, but it is a feature of the multisystem syndrome rather than the most specific unifying post-vaccine diagnosis.
Vaccine-associated myocarditis explains chest pain and troponin rise but ignores the systemic fever, rash, hepatosplenomegaly, kidney defects, and thrombocytopenia.
Late thrombocytopenia is one finding but not isolated/vaccine-induced immune thrombocytopenia; it does not explain coronary arteritis, kidney/hepatic lesions, or systemic inflammation.
Thrombocytopenia and D-dimer elevation are nonspecific; there is no schistocyte/MAHA evidence and cerebrenal or neurocognitive features are absent.
